Corollary
[Cylindrical strong maximum principle] Source: chow-et-al-ricci-flow-part-ii:page-0209 ↗ thm:euclidean-parabolic-strong-maximum-principle 1. ch12:12.42\group Strong Scalar Maximum Principles

If $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^n$ is connected and a subsolution as in Theorem 4.1 attains a nonnegative maximum at $(x_0,t_0)\in \Omega \times (0,T]$, then it equals that maximum on $\overline\Omega \times (0,t_0]$.

Proof

\sketch Every point of $\Omega \times (0,t_0]$ belongs to the closure of the backward reachable set of $(x_0,t_0)$; apply Theorem 4.1.

□
